articleHtml:
Whataburger Nutrition Calculator

Whataburger gives you far more control over a meal than the burger name alone suggests.

You can change the number of beef patties, add or remove cheese, bacon, jalapeños, avocado, vegetables, sauces, and other toppings. Then you can turn the entrée into a Whatameal with fries and a drink, choose onion rings instead, add dipping sauce, or finish with a shake.

Breakfast brings another set of choices, including Taquitos, Breakfast on a Bun, biscuits, pancakes, and the Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit.

The Whataburger Nutrition Calculator helps you put those pieces together and estimate the nutrition of the meal you actually order.

Use it to compare calories, protein, carbohydrates, total fat, saturated fat, sodium, fiber, sugar, cholesterol, and other available nutrition information across Whataburger menu items.

The Number of Burger Patties Makes a Huge Difference

Whataburger makes one nutrition comparison particularly easy to understand.

The original Whataburger is available with one, two, or three beef patties.

The current calculator lists approximately:

Whataburger: 590 calories

Double Meat Whataburger: 830 calories

Triple Meat Whataburger: 1,070 calories

The carbohydrate amount stays relatively similar because the bun and basic toppings remain similar.

What changes dramatically is the amount of beef.

As patties are added, protein increases, but calories, total fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, and sodium increase as well.

This makes patty count one of the most important decisions when estimating a Whataburger meal.

Single vs Double vs Triple Whataburger

If protein is your priority, a double or triple naturally gives you more than the standard burger.

The current calculator lists approximately:

  • Whataburger: 29 g protein
  • Double Meat Whataburger: 47 g protein
  • Triple Meat Whataburger: 65 g protein

But protein should not be considered by itself.

The triple also contains substantially more calories and fat than the single.

A more useful question is:

How much protein do I want from this meal, and how many calories do I want to use to get it?

For some people, the single plus a side will make sense.

For someone else, a double with a lighter side may work better.

Another person may prefer the triple as the main focus of the meal.

The calculator lets you compare those approaches directly.

A Whataburger Jr. Changes the Portion Before You Change the Recipe

You do not necessarily have to start removing ingredients to create a smaller meal.

The Whataburger Jr. gives you a smaller burger format from the beginning.

The current calculator lists it at approximately 310 calories.

That is nearly half the calories of the standard Whataburger in the current data.

This can be useful when you still want fries, onion rings, dessert, or another part of the meal.

Portion size often creates a much larger calorie difference than removing lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, or onions.

Cheese Is a Small-Looking Addition With a Real Nutrition Impact

Adding cheese affects several nutrients at once.

It contributes:

  • Calories
  • Protein
  • Total fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium

Cheese may only occupy a thin layer on the burger, but that does not mean its nutritional contribution is insignificant.

If you enjoy cheese, you do not have to remove it simply because you are tracking nutrition.

Just make sure your calculation represents the cheeseburger you actually eat rather than the plain burger.

Bacon and Cheese Change the Burger Quickly

The Bacon & Cheese Whataburger currently appears in the calculator at approximately 750 calories.

That is considerably higher than the standard Whataburger.

Bacon and cheese add flavor and protein, but they also increase fat, saturated fat, and sodium.

This is a useful example of how a couple of toppings can create a meaningful nutritional difference even when the bun and basic burger remain similar.

Jalapeños Add Flavor Differently

Jalapeños are very different from ingredients such as bacon, avocado, or cheese.

They can add substantial flavor without contributing many calories.

However, pickled or prepared peppers can contribute sodium.

This makes them a good example of why calories should not be the only nutrient you consider.

A topping can have almost no calorie impact but still matter if you are tracking sodium.

Avocado Changes More Than the Calorie Number

The Avocado Bacon Burger currently appears at approximately 820 calories in the calculator.

Avocado contributes calories and fat, but it also provides a very different type of food component than bacon or cheese.

Rather than automatically viewing avocado as something that needs to be removed, look at the complete meal.

If avocado is an ingredient you value, you might keep it and change something else.

Nutrition planning becomes much easier when you prioritize the foods you actually enjoy.

Vegetables Usually Have a Smaller Calorie Impact

Lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, and similar toppings generally make a much smaller contribution to calories than:

  • Beef patties
  • Cheese
  • Bacon
  • Avocado
  • Mayonnaise
  • Creamy sauces
  • Large buns

If you are trying to meaningfully reduce the calories in a burger, changing the major components will usually have a larger effect than removing vegetables.

Whataburger Is Made to Order

One of the most useful things about Whataburger is the ability to customize an order.

You can build a burger around your preferences instead of accepting only one fixed recipe.

That also means the standard menu nutrition number is only the starting point.

Removing mayonnaise can change the calories.

Adding cheese changes the calories.

Adding another patty changes them substantially.

Adding bacon, avocado, or another sauce changes them again.

Your final burger can therefore be quite different from the default version.

Do Not Forget Whatameal Sides

A Whataburger entrée and a Whatameal are not the same nutritional calculation.

Turning a burger or chicken sandwich into a meal generally adds:

a side

and

a beverage

Those two additions can contribute hundreds of calories.

If you are tracking your complete order, calculate the entrée first and then add the exact side and drink.

Fries Change Substantially With Size

The current calculator lists approximately:

Small French Fries: 270 calories

Medium French Fries: 400 calories

Large French Fries: 530 calories

That is a difference of about 260 calories between the small and large portions.

The burger did not change.

The side did.

This is one reason side size can be one of the easiest ways to adjust a Whatameal without changing the entrée you really want.

A Large Fry Can Be Nearly Another Entrée

A large order of fries currently contains more than 500 calories in the calculator.

That puts the side in the same general calorie range as some sandwiches.

Thinking of fries as "just a side" can therefore underestimate their role in the complete meal.

Always calculate the actual size.

Onion Rings Need Their Own Entry

If you choose onion rings instead of fries, do not use the fry nutrition value.

Onion rings have their own recipe, breading, frying process, serving size, calories, carbohydrates, and fat.

A side swap changes the meal even when the entrée remains exactly the same.

This makes Whatameal customization particularly useful for comparison.

Chicken Gives You Several Different Nutrition Profiles

Whataburger offers several chicken formats.

Current or commonly available options include items such as:

  • Whatachick’n Sandwich
  • Grilled Chicken Sandwich
  • Spicy Chicken Sandwich
  • Whatachick’n Strips
  • Chicken bites
  • Specialty chicken sandwiches

The word "chicken" alone does not tell you how many calories the item contains.

Preparation is one of the biggest reasons.

Grilled Chicken vs Crispy Chicken

The current calculator lists the Grilled Chicken Sandwich at approximately 430 calories.

The Whatachick’n Sandwich is around 540 calories, while the Spicy Chicken Sandwich is around 550 calories.

All three provide roughly 30 grams or more of protein in the current data.

The difference comes from preparation and the complete sandwich recipe.

Grilled chicken avoids breading and frying, which can reduce calories and fat compared with crispy options.

However, sauces, buns, and toppings still matter.

Protein Can Be Similar While Calories Differ

This is one of the most useful comparisons on the Whataburger menu.

The Grilled Chicken Sandwich currently provides roughly 32 grams of protein for around 430 calories.

The Whatachick’n Sandwich also provides roughly 32 grams of protein but has a higher calorie total in the current calculator.

That creates a different protein-to-calorie ratio.

If protein efficiency matters to you, compare:

Protein grams

against

Total calories

rather than selecting foods based only on which one contains chicken.

Chicken Strips Are Easy to Calculate by Piece Count

The current calculator lists three Whatachick’n Strips at approximately 460 calories.

Piece-based portions can be easier to track than sandwiches because you can count how many pieces you eat.

The bigger challenge comes from everything around them.

A strip meal may also include:

  • Fries
  • Texas toast
  • Gravy
  • Dipping sauce
  • A beverage

Those foods need to be included separately when you calculate the complete meal.

Dipping Sauce Can Matter More Than It Looks

Sauce containers are small, but their calorie contribution can be substantial depending on the sauce.

Whataburger is known for sauces and condiments such as:

  • Fancy Ketchup
  • Spicy Ketchup
  • Honey BBQ
  • Creamy Pepper
  • Honey Mustard
  • Ranch
  • Buffalo-style sauces
  • Gravy
  • Honey Butter

Different sauces contribute different combinations of fat, carbohydrates, sugar, and sodium.

If you use multiple containers, calculate multiple servings.

Honey BBQ Chicken Strip Sandwich Is a Good Example

The Honey BBQ Chicken Strip Sandwich is much more than chicken strips placed inside bread.

It combines breaded chicken strips with cheese, barbecue sauce, and Texas toast.

The current calculator lists it at approximately 890 calories.

It also provides substantial protein.

But the sandwich demonstrates how quickly several components can combine into a calorie-dense entrée.

If you turn it into a Whatameal, the side and drink need to be added on top of that.

The Patty Melt Has a Different Structure

The Whataburger Patty Melt is another item that deserves its own calculation.

It combines beef patties, cheese, grilled onions, Creamy Pepper Sauce, and Texas toast.

The current calculator lists it at approximately 940 calories.

That is very different from a basic Whataburger.

The Texas toast, multiple patties, cheese, and sauce all contribute to the final nutrition profile.

Do not estimate specialty burgers using the nutrition of the original Whataburger.

All-Time Favorites Are Full Recipes

Whataburger’s All-Time Favorites and specialty sandwiches often contain several ingredients beyond the standard burger.

Examples may include:

  • Multiple patties
  • Specialty cheese
  • Bacon
  • Grilled onions
  • Sweet sauces
  • Spicy sauces
  • Texas toast
  • Jalapeños

These foods should be treated as complete recipes.

The nutrition difference is not caused by one ingredient alone.

Sweet & Spicy Can Also Mean More Sugar

A sweet and spicy burger may contain sauces that contribute additional carbohydrates and sugar compared with a standard mustard-and-vegetable burger.

The current calculator lists the Sweet & Spicy Bacon Burger as one of the most calorie-dense items in its current dataset.

If you are tracking sugar or carbohydrates as well as calories, specialty sauces are worth checking.

Whataburger Breakfast Deserves Its Own Calculator

Breakfast at Whataburger is not just a smaller version of the lunch menu.

It has a distinct set of foods, including:

  • Taquitos with Cheese
  • Breakfast on a Bun
  • Biscuit sandwiches
  • Pancakes
  • Breakfast platters
  • Hash brown sticks
  • Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit
  • Other regional or current breakfast choices

Several breakfast items are customizable with different proteins.

The nutrition can therefore change considerably depending on what you choose.

Whataburger Breakfast Hours Matter

Breakfast is generally offered during designated overnight and morning hours rather than all day.

That makes breakfast its own menu occasion.

If you are comparing Whataburger breakfast calories, use breakfast-specific items instead of substituting lunch nutrition estimates.

Menu availability can vary by location.

Taquito With Cheese Can Change by Filling

A Whataburger Taquito with Cheese can be prepared with different fillings depending on availability.

Options may include:

  • Bacon
  • Sausage
  • Potato
  • Other market-specific fillings

The tortilla, egg, and cheese provide part of the nutrition.

The selected filling changes the rest.

A bacon Taquito and sausage Taquito should therefore not automatically share the same nutrition value.

Breakfast on a Bun Is a Complete Sandwich

The current calculator lists Breakfast on a Bun at approximately 510 calories for the represented configuration.

It combines bread, egg, cheese, and breakfast meat.

Those components explain why the sandwich can provide substantial protein while also contributing fat and sodium.

Make sure you select the version that corresponds to the protein you actually order.

Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit Is Sweet and Savory

The Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit is one of Whataburger’s signature breakfast items.

It combines a breaded chicken strip with a buttermilk biscuit and Honey Butter.

The current calculator lists it at approximately 580 calories.

Its calories come from several sources:

the biscuit,

fried chicken breading,

cooking fat,

and Honey Butter.

This means it has a very different macro profile from an egg-based breakfast sandwich even when the calorie totals appear somewhat similar.

Honey Butter Is Not Just a Flavoring

Honey Butter contributes sweetness and calories.

Because it combines a sweet component with fat, it can make a meaningful contribution to the final breakfast item.

If you add extra Honey Butter or use it separately, that additional serving should be counted when accurate tracking matters.

Biscuit Sandwiches Can Be Substantial

The current calculator lists a Biscuit Sandwich with Egg & Sausage at approximately 640 calories.

Biscuits themselves contain fat as part of their recipe.

Adding sausage, egg, and cheese creates a substantial breakfast.

If you then add hash browns and a sweetened beverage, breakfast can become much larger than the sandwich number alone suggests.

Sausage vs Bacon at Breakfast

Sausage and bacon are not nutritionally identical.

Sausage can contribute substantial calories and fat.

Bacon contributes its own fat and sodium.

When choosing between similar breakfast sandwiches, changing the breakfast meat can make a noticeable difference.

Calculate the exact configuration whenever possible.

Pancakes Need Their Toppings Counted

Pancakes may be served with additions such as butter and syrup.

Those extras contribute calories separately from the pancake itself.

If nutrition information breaks the components apart, include what you actually use.

Using all of the syrup is different from using half.

Skipping butter is different from adding extra.

The more customized the meal becomes, the more useful ingredient-level calculation becomes.

Hash Brown Sticks Are Part of the Meal Too

Breakfast sides can be easy to overlook because attention stays on the sandwich or Taquito.

Hash brown sticks are fried potato products and contribute calories, carbohydrates, and fat.

If you eat them with your breakfast, add them to the calculation.

Shakes Can Add Hundreds of Calories

Whataburger shakes should be treated as desserts or substantial beverages, not as calorie-free drinks.

The current calculator lists a small 16-ounce Vanilla Shake at approximately 410 calories.

Larger shakes can contain considerably more.

Flavors and seasonal recipes can also change the totals.

A shake alongside a large burger and fries can therefore make a major contribution to the complete meal.

Shake Size Matters More Than People Expect

Increasing shake size means adding more ice cream mixture.

Calories, carbohydrates, sugar, and fat rise accordingly.

If you are choosing a shake, make sure the serving size in the calculator matches the cup you order.

Do not use small-shake nutrition for a medium or large drink.

Vanilla, Chocolate, and Strawberry Are Not Necessarily Identical

Different shake flavors may have slightly different nutrition.

Flavor syrups, bases, and recipes can affect calories and sugar.

Seasonal shakes can differ even more.

Select the exact flavor whenever it is available instead of using a generic "Whataburger shake" estimate.

Cinnamon Roll Can Be a Substantial Dessert or Breakfast

The current calculator lists the Cinnamon Roll at approximately 580 calories.

It also contains a substantial amount of carbohydrates and sugar.

That places it closer to a full food item than a small extra.

If you eat a Cinnamon Roll with breakfast, include it as part of the meal.

If you have one after dinner, treat it as dessert.

Hot Apple Pie Gives You a Smaller Dessert Option

The current calculator lists the Hot Apple Pie at approximately 270 calories.

That is substantially less than the current Cinnamon Roll entry, although the two foods provide very different serving experiences.

Comparing dessert portions can be another way to adjust the total meal without changing your burger.

Sweetened Drinks Can Change Whatameal Calories Dramatically

A Whatameal often includes a fountain drink.

The nutrition difference between beverages can be enormous.

Water and many zero-sugar drinks contribute little or no energy.

Regular soft drinks and sweet tea can contribute significant calories and sugar, particularly in large cups.

That means two people can order the same burger and fries but end up with very different meal totals because of the drink.

Drink Size Is Particularly Important at Whataburger

Restaurant fountain drinks can be large.

As cup size increases, a sugar-sweetened beverage can contribute hundreds of additional calories.

If you order a regular soda or sweet tea, select the correct size.

If you refill the drink, your actual intake may be higher than one listed serving.

Coffee Is Very Different From a Shake

Plain brewed coffee contributes very few calories before additions.

A shake can contain hundreds.

This sounds obvious, but both appear in the beverage part of the menu.

The category does not determine the nutrition.

The actual drink does.

Looking for a Higher-Protein Whataburger Meal?

Several burgers and chicken items provide substantial amounts of protein.

The current calculator contains items with more than:

  • 30 grams of protein
  • 40 grams
  • 50 grams
  • Even 60 grams in large multi-patty burgers

But the larger burger is not automatically the most efficient protein choice.

Compare:

protein

with

total calories

and

saturated fat and sodium

A grilled chicken sandwich can provide a different protein-to-calorie ratio from a triple beef burger.

Looking for Fewer Calories?

Start with decisions that create the largest differences.

You could compare:

Whataburger Jr. vs regular Whataburger

Single vs double vs triple

Grilled chicken vs breaded chicken

Small fries vs large fries

Fries vs a lighter side

Regular soda vs a zero-calorie drink

No shake vs small shake

Standard burger vs calorie-dense specialty burger

You usually do not need to remove every topping.

Changing one major part of the order can make a much larger difference.

Trying to Reduce Carbohydrates?

Carbohydrates can come from multiple parts of a Whataburger order:

  • Hamburger buns
  • Texas toast
  • Chicken breading
  • Fries
  • Onion rings
  • Biscuits
  • Tortillas
  • Pancakes
  • Syrup
  • Honey Butter
  • Sweet sauces
  • Regular soda
  • Sweet tea
  • Shakes
  • Desserts

Removing a bun changes one source of carbohydrates, but the rest of the meal still matters.

Calculate the entire order.

Trying to Reduce Sodium?

Sodium can build quickly through:

  • Beef seasoning
  • Cheese
  • Bacon
  • Cured meats
  • Chicken breading
  • Sauces
  • Pickles
  • Jalapeños
  • Buns
  • Breakfast meats

Some specialty sandwiches contain a substantial amount before the side is added.

If sodium matters to you, check the combined meal rather than choosing solely from the calorie number.

Calories Do Not Tell You Everything

Consider two menu items with similar calories.

One may contain much more protein.

Another may provide more carbohydrates.

One may have considerably more sodium.

Another may contain more saturated fat or sugar.

This is why the Whataburger Nutrition Calculator shows more than calories.

Calories answer one question.

The rest of the nutrition panel answers others.

How to Calculate a Whatameal

Build the meal in four stages.

1. Choose your entrée

Select the exact burger, chicken sandwich, strips, breakfast item, or specialty sandwich.

2. Match the customization

Account for changes such as additional patties, cheese, bacon, avocado, or sauces when nutrition values are available.

3. Add the side

Choose the correct size of fries, onion rings, or another available side.

4. Add the beverage

Select the correct drink and size.

Then include dessert or dipping sauces if you have them.

This provides a much more realistic total than looking at the burger alone.

Example: Same Burger, Very Different Meal

Imagine starting with the standard Whataburger.

One order might include:

Whataburger
Small fries
Zero-sugar beverage

Another might include:

Whataburger
Large fries
Regular soda
Shake

Both people ordered the same burger.

Their complete meals are completely different nutritionally.

That is why the calculator should be used for the whole order.

Nutrition Information Disclaimer

Whataburger nutrition values are estimates based on standard recipes, published restaurant information, and listed serving sizes.

Actual values can vary because Whataburger meals are highly customizable. Changes to patties, cheese, bacon, sauces, vegetables, avocado, bread, sides, beverages, and other ingredients can alter the final nutrition significantly.

Recipes, ingredients, serving sizes, seasonal products, regional items, and menu availability may also change over time and by restaurant location.

Use the Whataburger Nutrition Calculator as a practical tool for comparing menu items and estimating your complete order rather than as an exact laboratory measurement.

People managing food allergies, celiac disease, diabetes, hypertension, kidney disease, or another condition that requires individualized nutrition management should verify current ingredient and allergen information with Whataburger and seek appropriate professional guidance when necessary.

faqs.q: Can I make Whataburger lower in calories?
faqs.a: Yes. Options include choosing a smaller burger, reducing patty count, selecting grilled instead of fried chicken, choosing a smaller side, modifying calorie-dense toppings, or selecting a low-calorie beverage.

faqs.q: Does removing the bun remove all carbohydrates?
faqs.a: No. Sauces, breaded chicken, fries, onion rings, sweet beverages, and other foods can still contribute carbohydrates.

faqs.q: Can I calculate an entire Whatameal?
faqs.a: Yes. Add the entrée, modifications, side, beverage, sauces, and dessert to estimate the nutrition of the complete meal.
